From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Dedicated sizing draft — quick math and assumptions

Hi all — I ran the traffic through our throughput model. Notes, assumptions and the resulting recommended slab below. I kept things explicit so procurement can see the reasoning.

Assumptions (conservative):
- Peak: 4,500 requests/min = 75 req/s.
- Average tokens per request: 220 tokens (from Liam's CSV).
- Peak tokens/sec = 75 * 220 = 16,500 tokens/sec.
- Target p95 generation latency <= 300ms for interactive route (end-to-end p95 target assumes network + decode + overhead; we budget 200–220ms for model inference).
- Primary model: redwood-7b-quant (recommended for cost/quality balance). We profile two GPU SKUs: H100 and A100-80GB.

Empirical throughput estimates (profiled with Redwood runtime, continuous batching, KV prefix cache warm):
- H100 (opt kernels, batch window 8–12ms): ~3,500 tokens/sec per GPU (single-model serving for redwood-7b-quant).
- A100-80GB (same config): ~1,800 tokens/sec per GPU.

Baseline GPU math:
- Required GPUs (baseline, no headroom) for 16,500 tokens/sec:
  - H100: ceil(16,500 / 3,500) = 5 GPUs.
  - A100: ceil(16,500 / 1,800) = 10 GPUs.

Recommended reserved slab (production-ready, includes headroom):
- We recommend a 50% operational headroom to absorb short bursts, KV cache churn, and degraded perf during maintenance.
  - H100 reserved slab = 5 * 1.5 -> 7.5 => round up to 8 GPUs.
  - A100 reserved slab = 10 * 1.5 -> 15 GPUs.

Latency implications (p95):
- With H100 slab (8 GPUs), expected model inference p95: ~160–210ms (model inference only). End-to-end p95 estimate ~240–280ms (includes network + decode).
- With A100 slab (15 GPUs), expected model inference p95: ~220–300ms, end-to-end p95 ~280–350ms (risk to the 300ms target).

Operational recommendations / fallbacks:
1) Primary: H100 dedicated slab 8 GPUs for guaranteed SLO compliance.
2) Fallback path: if customer wants lower committed dollars, propose hybrid: reserved A100 slab (10 GPUs) + burst-able H100 pool for peak spikes (2–3 H100 instances). This preserves steady-state cost control while protecting p95.
3) Canary deploy with a 10% traffic shadow to the reserved slab for 48 hours, verify p95 and error rates.
4) KV cache warmup plan: preheat prefixes for the top 500 queries; expect a 10–15% token/sec uplift after warm.
5) Autoscale policy: keep max concurrency per server conservative and prefer sub-second batch windows to prioritize latency.

Cost note (very rough): we’ll surface costs next — Jordan will pull list pricing for committed vs burst hours.

Ben
Lead — Inference Ops, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: procurement@mercury-analytics.com, irene_choi@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-16T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing draft — quick math and assumptions

Hi — answering the ops questions so procurement has language to review.

Maintenance and availability notes:
- Rolling maintenance model: we schedule staggered driver/kernel updates with a 3-node frequency plan. For an 8 GPU H100 slab (typically 4-8 servers), we expect <0.5% impact to availability during planned maintenance if canaries and warm caches are used.
- p95 impact during maintenance: expect 1.05x–1.2x model inference p95 for short windows (5–20 minutes) if the slab is operating at >70% capacity. That’s why recommended slab includes 50% headroom.

SLO / SLA credit guidance (draft language):
- Target: p95 <= 300ms for the interactive route.
- Measurement: rolling 30-day window, excluding scheduled maintenance with 48-hour prior notice and agreed maintenance windows.
- Credit trigger: if monthly rolling p95 > 350ms for interactive route, credit = 10% of monthly committed fee for that month. (This is a negotiable starting point.)

Canary and preheat checklist (operations):
- Shadow 10% for 48h, then ramp 25% for 12h, then cutover.
- Pre-warm KV cache for top prefixes and warm embeddings cache for user-id signals; preheat automation script provided in Drive link.

Link: https://drive.redwood.com/merc-mercury/throughput-model-v1

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
